# KORTEX

> KORTEX is a GEO, SEO and content creation studio based in Fès, Morocco, serving clients worldwide. A client provides one source (a blog post, YouTube video, podcast episode or webinar) and KORTEX turns it into up to 30+ assets built to be cited by AI answer engines such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews and Claude, and ranked by search engines. Expertise is extracted from the client's own content, never invented, and a person reviews everything before publication.

## Plans
- GHOST: €2,500 per month. 1 source per month, 10 assets per source, monthly citation check on 10 buyer questions, delivery in 5 business days.
- SWARM: €5,500 per month. 1 source per month, 20 to 24 assets per source, schema markup and internal linking, monthly citation check on 10 buyer questions, monthly strategy call.
- TITAN: from €12,000 per month. 2 or more sources per month, 28 or more assets per source, full citation tracking with competitors, off-site authority work, delivery in 3 to 4 business days.
- Every plan: no setup fees, month to month with 30 days' notice, the client owns 100% of the content.

Founder: Hamza Bentarhlia. Contact: contact@kortexlab.me. Book a strategy call: https://cal.com/hamza-bentarhlia

## Glossary
- [Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/answer-engine-optimization/): Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) shapes content so it is chosen as the direct answer by assistants, snippets and AI engines. How it relates to GEO.
- [Answer-first content](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/answer-first-content/): Answer-first content opens each page or section with a direct, complete answer before adding detail. Why AI engines quote it more easily.
- [Citation](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/citation/): A citation is the link an AI answer shows to its source. How it differs from being named, why it matters, and how to log it.
- [Citation rate](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/citation-rate/): Citation rate is the share of tracked questions for which an AI engine names or links your brand in its answer. How it is measured and why it varies.
- [Content decay](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/content-decay/): Content decay is the slow loss of accuracy, relevance and visibility of a page over time. Why it matters for citations and how to review.
- [E-E-A-T](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/e-e-a-t/): E-E-A-T stands for experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trustworthiness. What Google says it is, what it is not, and how to show it on a B2B site.
- [Entity](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/entity/): An entity is a person, company, product, place or concept that a machine can identify without ambiguity. Why consistent entities help AI engines cite you.
- [Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/generative-engine-optimization/): Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) structures content so AI answer engines can understand it, quote it and name you as the source. Definition, examples.
- [Google AI Overviews](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/ai-overviews/): Google AI Overviews are AI-written summaries shown at the top of some Google results, with links to the sources used. How they affect visibility.
- [Grounding](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/grounding/): Grounding anchors an AI answer in retrieved, checkable sources. Why answers show citations, and what it means for your pages.
- [hreflang](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/hreflang/): hreflang tells search engines which language or regional version of a page to show to which user. The rules, an example and the common mistake.
- [Information gain](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/information-gain/): Information gain is what a page adds that other pages on the topic do not. How it relates to originality, and what adds it in practice.
- [Knowledge graph](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/knowledge-graph/): A knowledge graph stores entities and the relationships between them. What it is, how it relates to your site, and what you can and cannot control.
- [llms.txt](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/llms-txt/): llms.txt is a proposed plain-text file at the root of a website that gives language models a short description of the site and links to its best pages.
- [Prompt-level demand](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/prompt-level-demand/): Prompt-level demand is the range of full questions people put to AI assistants about a topic. How to estimate it when no engine publishes volumes.
- [Query fan-out](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/query-fan-out/): Query fan-out is when an AI search system turns one question into several related searches. Why it matters for how you structure your content.
- [Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/retrieval-augmented-generation/): Retrieval-augmented generation lets an AI model fetch relevant, current pages before it writes an answer. How it works and what it means for your content.
- [Schema markup](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/schema-markup/): Schema markup is structured data that tells machines what a page contains: an article, a product, an FAQ, an organization. Why it helps AI and search.
- [Search Engine Optimization (SEO)](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/search-engine-optimization/): Search Engine Optimization (SEO) makes pages easy for search engines to crawl, understand and rank. Why it still matters when AI engines answer questions.
- [Share of model](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/share-of-model/): Share of model is a loose term for how often an AI model names or cites a brand compared with others. A plain way to compute it.
- [Topical authority](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/topical-authority/): Topical authority is the degree to which search and AI engines see a site as a reliable source on a subject, built by covering it deeply and consistently.
- [Zero-click search](https://www.kortexlab.me/glossary/zero-click-search/): Zero-click search is a search that ends on the results page or in the answer, with no visit to a site. What it changes for content.

## Comparisons
- [KORTEX vs a freelance writer](https://www.kortexlab.me/compare/kortex-vs-freelance-writer/): A good freelancer writes good articles. KORTEX delivers a structured month of content across formats, shaped for AI citation. When each one fits.
- [KORTEX vs an SEO agency](https://www.kortexlab.me/compare/kortex-vs-seo-agency/): An SEO agency improves rankings. KORTEX builds content from your expertise and structures it for AI citations, SEO included. When each one fits.
- [KORTEX vs doing it yourself with ChatGPT](https://www.kortexlab.me/compare/kortex-vs-chatgpt/): ChatGPT can draft content for a few euros a month. It does not extract your expertise, check facts, keep formats consistent or track citations. Compared.
- [KORTEX vs hiring an in-house writer](https://www.kortexlab.me/compare/kortex-vs-in-house-writer/): An in-house writer knows your company and is always there. KORTEX brings a pipeline and a monthly citation check. How they differ and when to hire.

- [How to build a category in the age of AI search.](https://www.kortexlab.me/blog/category-creation-ai-search/): Category creation in AI search means publishing a precise definition before ChatGPT or Perplexity writes one for you. A four-phase B2B playbook.
